rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Keep the gradient fixed and raise temperature to test selectivity in the crowded central cluster. The last peak is already comfortably below 10 minutes, so resolving the critical pairs is the priority.

Make the gradient shallower at the best temperature so far to expand separation of the remaining critical pair. The current 6.77-minute last peak leaves room to improve resolution without incurring a time penalty.

The shallower gradient worsened the closest pair, suggesting selectivity rather than peak spacing is limiting. Test 55 C to shift that selectivity, with a 12-minute gradient to protect neighboring separations while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.
Injection 4 reached the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark. Shorten the gradient by one step to test whether full resolution can be preserved with faster elution.

The shorter gradient compromised a neighboring pair, so restore the successful 12-minute duration and increase the starting organic fraction by one step. This tests faster elution through a narrower gradient window while retaining injection 4 as the fully resolved benchmark.

Retain injection 4 as the maximum-score benchmark and explore a faster, higher-temperature regime. The central pairs show different temperature responses, so this tests whether a selectivity reversal can restore separation under a substantially steeper gradient.

Explore lower-temperature selectivity while retaining injection 4 as the maximum-score benchmark. Cooling may separate the central cluster in a different elution order, and the broad 10-minute gradient should leave room before the time penalty begins.

Test a higher starting organic fraction at 60 C to shift selectivity in the reordered central cluster, while lengthening the gradient from six to eight minutes to improve spacing. Injection 4 remains the maximum-score fallback as we search for a faster fully resolved method.

Increase the starting organic fraction one step to test whether the remaining central pair separates further in the high-temperature elution order. Monitor the first pair closely, since stronger initial solvent will compress early peaks; injection 4 remains the fully resolved benchmark.

Return to the successful low-start, 55 C regime and use the endpoint to refine gradient slope between injections 4 and 5. This tests whether a modestly steeper slope than the fully resolved benchmark can preserve all separations while reducing elution time.

At the higher starting fraction, slightly flatten the gradient relative to injection 6 to recover its under-resolved central pair. This may retain full resolution with more balanced critical-pair margins and a last-peak time near the successful benchmark.

Lower the endpoint one more step to bring injection 12’s R=1.47 pair above 1.5 while preserving its other critical separation. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially matching the maximum CRF with better resolution margins.

With two maximum-score methods secured, test whether a steeper gradient at 60 C moves the central cluster into a better-separated elution order. This probes a substantially faster regime while avoiding the early-peak compression seen at high starting organic fraction.

Preserve injection 4’s successful gradient slope and temperature, but end the ramp earlier at 0.65 organic. Since all peaks previously eluted by 7.60 minutes, this should retain maximum CRF while shortening the programmed gradient.

Test whether a steeper gradient at 40 C improves selectivity in the central cluster, whose elution pattern differs from the high-temperature runs. This explores another route to faster full resolution while retaining the established maximum-score methods.

Test whether a shallower gradient at 60 C restores separation of the temperature-sensitive central pair while preserving the other separations. The last peak is expected near, but below, 10 minutes, offering another potential maximum-score method.

Return to the successful 55 C regime and test one shallower-gradient step to map the resolution margin around injection 4. This should improve the earlier critical pair, while checking whether the later pair remains above 1.5 before the last peak reaches 10 minutes.

Combine a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient to balance the two critical separations at 55 C. This tests whether the later pair gains resolution without sacrificing the earlier pair, while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Refine around the fully resolved injection 13 with a slightly shallower slope and a stronger endpoint. This should preserve both critical separations and keep the last peak below 10 minutes, testing a nearby maximum-score method with useful resolution margins.

Test a small slope reduction from injection 4, between the fully resolved 12-minute gradient and the slightly under-resolved 14-minute gradient. This targets improved balance between the two critical pairs while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Use a slope between injections 12 and 13 to target full resolution with a slightly earlier last peak than injection 13. The 0.75 endpoint remains above the organic fraction at which the last peak eluted in those runs.

Preserve the successful gradient slope through the crowded cluster, then switch to a lower-organic hold. This tests whether a shorter programmed ramp can retain full resolution and elute the last compound before 10 minutes, although the hold may delay that peak.

Flatten the gradient from injection 19 to improve its remaining R=1.10 pair while exploiting the larger margin in the later critical pair. This targets a more comfortably resolved maximum-score alternative, with the last peak expected below 10 minutes; injection 4 remains the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Raise the endpoint one step from injection 24 to accelerate elution while spending some of its resolution margin. This final refinement targets full resolution with a shorter last-peak time; injection 4 remains the fastest demonstrated maximum-score method.
